description: Frozen synthetic family-1 (fde-db-triage) playthrough for the P3.2 drift-boundary assertion. Exercises every detector tier live at DETECTOR_VERSION 2: agnostic (queries, deliverable, AI, messages), verification (L4 defense), fde-db-triage-specific (dedup / status-filter / figures-match), the product-sense fork (curveball + reasoning + protected deliverable), and an integrity.* event that must stay filtered out. DO NOT EDIT: verify-family1-drift-inert.ts re-runs the full detector pipeline over this stream and asserts the emitted units are byte-identical to baseline-units-v2.json modulo the detector_version stamp.

payload.text: Before I dig in — which report shows the wrong number, and what figure did you expect to see?
can't just ship the raw sum — the webhook retries double-count ~8% of succeeded payments and overstate revenue; the board needs the reconciled number.

payload.sql: WITH dedup AS (SELECT MIN(id) AS id FROM payments WHERE status = 'succeeded' GROUP BY external_payment_id) SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', created_at) AS month, SUM(amount_cents) FROM payments WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM dedup) AND status = 'succeeded' GROUP BY month
SELECT external_payment_id, COUNT(*) FROM payments WHERE status = 'succeeded' GROUP BY external_payment_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

payload.text: What's the idiomatic SQLite pattern to dedup rows sharing external_payment_id, keeping the earliest id?
Walk me through how you derived the corrected April figure.
I deduped by external_payment_id keeping MIN(id), filtered to status = 'succeeded', then summed amount_cents per month — April dropped by the 26 duplicate rows' value.

data.root_cause_finding: A webhook-retry bug double-inserted ~8% of succeeded payments in April and May; duplicates share external_payment_id.
data.client_facing_summary: Revenue was overstated by duplicate webhook inserts; corrected figures attached.
data.decisions_and_tradeoffs: Deduped by external_payment_id (MIN(id)) and filtered to succeeded before summing; declined the raw-sum shortcut because it overstates the board number.
